definitions.explanation: What is actually the case; the real state of affairs.

examples.japanese: {真実|しんじつ}を{明|あき}らかにする。
{真実|しんじつ}の{愛|あい}を{見|み}つけた。

notes:
{真実|しんじつ} means truth or reality — the actual state of affairs, especially when it has been hidden or unknown. Composed of {真|しん} (true) + {実|じつ} (reality).

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {真実|しんじつ}を{知|し}る: to learn the truth
- {真実|しんじつ}を{明|あき}らかにする: to reveal the truth
- {真実|しんじつ}を{隠|かく}す: to hide the truth
- {真実|しんじつ}の{愛|あい}: true love
- {真実|しんじつ}に{迫|せま}る: to get close to the truth

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {事実|じじつ}: fact (objective, verifiable)
- {本当|ほんとう}: truth, really (everyday)
- {真理|しんり}: universal/philosophical truth
- {実態|じったい}: actual state, reality (of a situation)

NUANCE:
{真実|しんじつ} often implies something deeper or hidden that needs to be uncovered. {事実|じじつ} is more neutral and factual. {本当|ほんとう} is the everyday word for "truth" or "really."
